text.p: Headlines from major national newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
EL PAIS
- Chlorine leak causes panick in northern Madrid.
- Critics blame Basque police for not dealing more effectively with violence in Basque Country.
EL MUNDO
- Government pressures Basque police to be more effective against violence.
- Two well dressed people, a car and a coffin are sufficient to create a funeral palour, according to liberalisation decree due to be approved by government.
DIARIO 16
- Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar personally supports government spokesman Miguel Angel Rodriguez before a group headed by Deputy Prime Minister Rodrigo Rato who demand he resign.
ABC
- Panick and chaos erupt in northern Madrid after toxic leak from laboratory.
CINCO DIAS
- Banco Santander sells 14.3 percent stake in sugar group Ebro to France's Generale Sucriere for 17.1 billion pesetas.
- Electricity group Endesa, passing through 10,000 peseta barrier on bourse which once again reached historic highs on Monday, is diamond in the crown.
EXPANSION
- One in four families saves through investment funds.
- Fernando Abril finalises his involvement in Telefonica as finance director.
- NH Hotels challenges Hilton and launches offer for Madrid hotel Eurobuilding.
GACETA DE LOS NEGOCIOS
- Government measures to boost consumption will have little real impact.
- Mariano Gomez de Liano and Francisco Javier Sitges will be called to declare in Conde case at the end of January.
